chapters.title: Chapter 6: Applying the Framework, Positioning Across the Cycle

lessons.title: Reading the Indicators: A Practical Checklist for Locating Any Economy in Its Debt Cycle

body.text: Chapter 5 built a five-question scorecard for India specifically. This lesson strips out everything India-specific and turns it into a universal checklist, with a simple numeric score, that you can apply to any economy in the world.

children.text: Every framework in this course maps onto one of five questions, and every one of those questions can be asked of any economy, not just India. This lesson generalises Chapter 5's scorecard into a repeatable process with an actual numeric score, then tests that process against a case this course has already studied in hindsight, the United States in 2007, to show it would have flagged real risk before the event most people remember it for.
The Universal Scorecard: Five Questions, Any Economy

body.caption: The five questions and where to find the data for any economy

cells: Force One
Is growth still productivity and demographics-driven, or increasingly debt-propped?
National statistics office GDP data; UN Population Division demographic projections
MP1-MP2-MP3 Progression
How much conventional monetary room does the central bank have left?
The central bank's own policy rate history and balance sheet size, published directly by most central banks
Three Debt Stocks
Are government, household, and corporate debt-to-GDP at mature-cycle extremes?
IMF Global Debt Database, BIS credit statistics, or the country's own central bank financial stability report
Seven Bubble Indicators
Is a broad, multi-asset bubble building right now?
Valuation multiples, leverage proxies, and sentiment data for the specific assets in question, applying Chapter 2's Lesson 2 checklist directly
Currency Composition
How much of the debt is local-currency and locally held versus foreign-currency or foreign-held?
IMF Article IV consultations, World Bank International Debt Statistics, or the country's own external debt reports

children.text: Turning It Into a Number: The Cycle Stage Score

Score each of the five dimensions from 0 to 2, where 0 signals early-cycle conditions with room to run, 1 signals mid-cycle, and 2 signals late-cycle conditions consistent with the mature economies in Chapter 4's case studies. Summing all five gives a total out of 10.

cells: Force One
Growing, young workforce; growth tracks productivity
Workforce growth slowing; growth partly debt-supported
Ageing or shrinking workforce; growth reliant on asset prices
MP1-MP2-MP3
Policy rate well above zero, real room to cut
Policy rate low, limited room left, no MP2 yet
At or near zero; MP2 or MP3 already in active use
Three Debt Stocks
Debt-to-GDP moderate and stable or falling
One or more stocks rising meaningfully from a moderate base
One or more stocks at or near historical or cross-country highs
Seven Bubble Indicators
0-2 of 7 present in any major asset
3-4 of 7 present in at least one major asset
5 or more of 7 present in one or more major assets
Currency Composition
Debt almost entirely local-currency, locally held
A meaningful minority is foreign-currency or foreign-held
A large share is foreign-currency-denominated or foreign-held

body.label: How to Read the Total Score
body.value: 0-3: Early Cycle · 4-6: Mid Cycle · 7-10: Late Cycle
body.context: These bands are a starting heuristic, not a precise scientific threshold; treat a score near a boundary as a prompt to look closer, not a firm verdict

children.text: Worked Example: Scoring the US in 2007

body.caption: Applying the scorecard to the US, using only information available at the time

cells: Force One
Growth still tracked reasonable productivity trends, though some of it was already wealth-effect driven from rising home values
MP1-MP2-MP3
The Fed funds rate sat around 5.25%, well above zero but already lower than the peaks of prior cycles covered in Chapter 2's Lesson 1's declining-peak pattern
Three Debt Stocks
US household debt-to-income was at a record high, as covered in Chapter 4's Lesson 3, a clear late-cycle signal on this dimension alone
Seven Bubble Indicators
US housing showed 5 or more of Dalio's seven indicators clearly, exactly as scored in Chapter 4's Lesson 3
Currency Composition
US debt was, and remains, dollar-denominated and benefits from reserve currency status, a structurally favourable score

body.label: US 2007 Total Score
body.context: Sitting at the upper edge of mid-cycle, bordering on late-cycle, using only information genuinely available before the crisis unfolded

body.text: A score of 6, driven almost entirely by two dimensions, the debt stock and bubble checklist both reading late-cycle, would have been a legitimate, non-hindsight-dependent signal to scrutinise US housing and household leverage closely in 2007, well before Lehman's collapse the following year. This does not mean the scorecard predicts an exact date or trigger; it means a structured process would have flagged real risk building using only data that existed at the time.

children.text: Limitations: What This Scorecard Cannot Tell You

A high score identifies elevated risk, not a specific date or trigger. The US housing bubble showed several of Dalio's seven indicators for roughly two to three years before the actual credit event in 2007-2008, and an investor who acted purely on a high score alone in 2005 would have missed substantial further gains before the eventual turn. The scorecard also cannot fully quantify how well policymakers will respond once a credit event does happen, which is precisely why Chapter 4 dedicated separate case studies to the same starting conditions producing very different outcomes depending on the response. Use this scorecard to identify where scrutiny belongs, not as a precise, mechanical timing signal.

body.title: Score an Economy of Your Choice
steps: Pick any economy other than India or the US, one you follow or one relevant to your portfolio
Score each of the five dimensions from 0 to 2 using current, primary-source data, not secondhand commentary
Sum the five scores and note which band, early, mid, or late cycle, the total falls into
Identify which single dimension contributed the most to the total score, and what specific data point you would watch next to see whether that dimension is improving or worsening
Revisit your score in six months and note what changed

body.title: Calculate a Total Score
body.prompt: An economy scores as follows: Force One = 1, MP1-MP2-MP3 = 2, Three Debt Stocks = 2, Seven Bubble Indicators = 1, Currency Composition = 0. What is the total Cycle Stage Score out of 10?
body.explanation: 1 + 2 + 2 + 1 + 0 equals 6, placing this economy at the upper edge of mid-cycle, close to the late-cycle threshold, driven mainly by an exhausted monetary policy dimension and elevated debt stocks, similar in shape to this lesson's US 2007 worked example.

body.title: Check Your Understanding
body.question: In the US 2007 worked example, which two dimensions contributed the most to pushing the total score toward the late-cycle range?
options: The Three Debt Stocks dimension and the Seven Bubble Indicators dimension
All five dimensions contributed exactly equally
body.explanation: Both the Three Debt Stocks dimension, driven by record US household debt-to-income, and the Seven Bubble Indicators dimension, driven by the housing bubble scoring 5 or more of Dalio's seven signs, scored the maximum of 2 in this example, together accounting for 4 of the total 6 points and correctly flagging where the real risk was concentrated.

body.text: This lesson presents a general educational scoring framework for identifying debt cycle stage and is not investment advice or a market forecast. The scoring bands are a teaching heuristic, not an empirically validated predictive model, and should be used to prioritise further research, not as a standalone trading or allocation signal. The US 2007 worked example uses figures already presented and sourced in Chapter 4's Lesson 3.

points: Chapter 5's India-specific scorecard generalises into five questions applicable to any economy: Force One, the MP1-MP2-MP3 progression, the three debt stocks, the seven bubble indicators, and currency composition
Scoring each dimension 0 to 2 and summing gives a Cycle Stage Score out of 10, with rough bands for early, mid, and late cycle, used as a heuristic rather than a precise threshold

Applied retrospectively to the US in 2007, using only information available at the time, the scorecard produces a score of 6, correctly flagging elevated risk concentrated in household debt and the housing bubble before the 2008 crisis unfolded
The scorecard identifies where risk is concentrated, not when a credit event will occur or how well policymakers will respond once it does, both genuine limitations worth remembering
The next lesson applies this same cycle-stage thinking directly to asset allocation, covering how equities, gold, bonds, and cash tend to behave differently at each stage
